title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: Guest User (EE2) shares a unique identifier (e.g., email, phone number) with the Home Hub (P1) to unlock the door. This identifier is globally unique and can be used to link the Guest to the Home Hub, enabling the Hub to identify the Guest's identity.
assumptions: The Guest User has a unique identifier that is known or discoverable by the Home Hub.

title: Identifiable Information via Identifier
description: The Guest User (EE2) provides identifiable information (e.g., a unique identifier) to the Home Hub (P1). This information is processed by the Hub, allowing the Hub to identify the Guest's identity.
assumptions: The identifier provided by the Guest is unique and sufficient to identify the Guest.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Guest User (EE2) shares personal data (e.g., email, phone number) with the Home Hub (P1). This data is highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required, but it is being shared unnecessarily for the purpose of unlocking a door.
assumptions: The data type (e.g., email) is considered highly sensitive and should not be shared for this purpose.

title: Lawful Processing of Personal Data
description: The Guest User (EE2) processes personal data (e.g., email) in a way that may not be lawful. Sharing personal data for the purpose of unlocking a door may not have a valid legal basis, such as valid consent or a legitimate interest.
assumptions: The Guest User does not have valid consent or a legitimate legal basis for sharing this personal data.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). If the Home Hub uses a unique identifier (e.g., a specific sensor ID, device fingerprint, or unique event code) to identify the data subject, this creates a direct link between the data and the individual. This is a genuine threat because the data flow explicitly involves writing events to a log, and if the identifier is unique to the subject, the data is effectively linked to the individual.
assumptions: The Home Hub uses a unique identifier to identify the data subject.

title: Identifying via Identifier
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). If the Home Hub uses a unique identifier (e.g., a specific sensor ID, device fingerprint, or unique event code) to identify the data subject, this creates a direct link between the data and the individual. This is a genuine threat because the data flow explicitly involves writing events to a log, and if the identifier is unique to the subject, the data is effectively identified.
assumptions: The Home Hub uses a unique identifier to identify the data subject.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). Motion, door, and sensor events are typically considered highly sensitive personal data. If the Home Hub processes this data without strict necessity, it violates the data minimization principle (Nc.1.1.2). This is a genuine threat because the data flow involves processing sensitive data types (motion, door, sensor events) which are often considered highly sensitive.
assumptions: Motion, door, and sensor events are considered highly sensitive personal data.

title: Lawful Processing Issues
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). If the processing of this data is not lawful (e.g., lacks valid consent, incorrect lawful ground, or automated decision making on sensitive data), it violates privacy standards. This is a genuine threat because the data flow involves processing sensitive personal data, and if the processing is not lawful, it constitutes a non-compliance threat.
assumptions: The processing of motion/door/sensor events by the Home Hub may not be lawful.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). If the data subject (or the user) is not aware that their motion, door, or sensor data is being collected, processed, or stored, this creates a significant privacy risk. This is a genuine threat because the data flow involves processing sensitive personal data, and if the data subject is unaware of this processing, it violates the principle of awareness.
assumptions: The data subject is not aware that their motion, door, or sensor data is being processed by the Home Hub.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure
description: The Home Hub (P1) writes motion/door/sensor events to the Local Event Log (DS1). If the data is implicitly collected as a side-effect of the data flow (e.g., the act of writing the event to the log reveals metadata about the user's behavior or location), this constitutes implicit data disclosure. This is a genuine threat because the data flow involves processing sensitive personal data, and if the data is implicitly disclosed, it violates the data minimization principle.
assumptions: The act of writing motion/door/sensor events to the log may reveal additional personal data not functionally needed.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares camera clips using a unique identifier (e.g., camera ID, user ID) to link the data to a specific individual. This allows the Cloud Video Storage (DS2) to potentially identify the data subject.
assumptions: The camera clips contain a unique identifier that is not removed or obfuscated before sharing.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) shares personal data (camera clips) of a specific individual. The data type is highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required, but it is being shared unnecessarily.
assumptions: The camera clips contain personal data that is not functionally required for the video storage system.

title: Excessive Exposure to Predetermined Parties
description: The Cloud Video Storage (DS2) receives the camera clips and makes them accessible to a predetermined set of parties (e.g., the Home Hub, the cloud provider, or other authorized entities). This amplifies the potential risk of data exposure.
assumptions: The data is published or broadcasted by the system to external parties beyond the functional scope.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or motion event ID). This allows the backend to link the alert to a specific individual or device, enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The motion alert contains a unique identifier that is globally or locally unique.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the identifier is unique as stated in the threat-tree node L.1.1.

title: Identifying via Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert using an identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID) that uniquely identifies the data subject. This allows the mobile app backend to identify the specific individual receiving the alert.
assumptions: The identifier used is a unique reference to the data subject.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the identifier is a unique reference as stated in the threat-tree node I.2.1.1.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub forwards personal data (motion alert) to the mobile app backend. The alert may contain sensitive personal data (e.g., health, location, or behavioral data) that is processed beyond what is strictly functionally required for the basic forwarding function.
assumptions: The motion alert contains sensitive personal data types.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the alert contains sensitive personal data as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.1.1.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend. The volume of personal data (the alert itself) is processed beyond what is functionally needed for the basic forwarding function.
assumptions: The motion alert constitutes personal data that is processed.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the alert is considered personal data as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.2.1.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert to the mobile app backend. The processing and treatment of the personal data (the alert) is not necessary to achieve the functional goal of simply forwarding the alert.
assumptions: The forwarding of the alert is not functionally dependent on further processing or treatment of the alert data.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the forwarding is not functionally dependent on further processing as stated in the threat-tree node Dd.3.1.

title: GDPR Noncompliance (Data Minimization)
description: The Home Hub forwards personal data (motion alert) to the mobile app backend. This may violate the data minimization principle of GDPR, as the alert may contain more personal data than is strictly functionally required for the basic forwarding function.
assumptions: The motion alert contains personal data that is not strictly necessary for the basic forwarding function.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the alert contains personal data as stated in the threat-tree node Nc.1.1.2.

title: GDPR Noncompliance (Metadata Impacting Deniability)
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert to the mobile app backend. Metadata associated with the alert may contain unintended data that impacts deniability claims about the alert's origin or content.
assumptions: Metadata associated with the alert may contain unintended data impacting deniability claims.
uncertainty_note: Assuming metadata impacts deniability claims as stated in the threat-tree node Nr.1.3.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains a unique identifier (e.g., a user ID or device ID) that links the data to a specific individual. This allows the backend to link the notification to the specific homeowner, enabling the homeowner to be identified or targeted based on this unique identifier.
assumptions: The notification includes a unique identifier that is globally or locally unique to the homeowner.

title: Identifying via Identifier
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains a unique identifier (e.g., a user ID or device ID) that is used to identify the data subject. This identifier allows the system to process or store data that is directly linked to the homeowner's identity.
assumptions: The notification includes a unique identifier that is used to identify the data subject.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains personal data (motion-detected data) that is highly sensitive. This data type is collected and processed without strict functional necessity, as the system may be able to achieve its goals without this specific type of data.
assumptions: The notification contains personal data that is highly sensitive and not strictly required for the system's functionality.

title: Lawfulness Problems Not Related to Consent
description: The mobile app backend pushes a motion-detected notification to the homeowner's phone. The notification contains personal data (motion-detected data) that is processed without a valid lawful ground, such as consent. The system may be processing this data under a legal ground that is not explicitly stated or valid.
assumptions: The notification contains personal data processed under a legal ground that is not valid or explicitly stated.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend shares aggregated device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor. The analytics data contains unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, user IDs) that allow the vendor to link and identify the specific individuals whose data is being shared.
assumptions: The analytics data includes unique identifiers that are not stripped or obfuscated before sharing.

title: Excessive Exposure to Predetermined Parties
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) receives the aggregated device-usage analytics. The vendor is a predetermined external party, and the data is shared with this specific vendor rather than being broadcasted or made broadly accessible to a large, dynamic set of parties.
assumptions: The vendor is a known, targeted entity, not a general public or broad audience.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The mobile app backend (P2) processes device-usage analytics that contain identifiable information (e.g., unique identifiers). The system requests and processes this data, which allows the vendor to derive the identity of the data subjects.
assumptions: The analytics data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The mobile app backend retrieves a stored video clip using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or video hash) from the data store. This identifier allows the backend to link the video data to a specific individual or device, enabling the homeowner to identify the source of the video.
assumptions: The video clip is associated with a unique identifier that is globally or locally unique.

title: Linking via Quasi-identifier
description: The data flow transmits metadata about the parties involved in the retrieval process. This metadata may include information about the mobile app's identity, the homeowner's identity, or the video's metadata, which can be used to link the data flow to specific individuals or devices.
assumptions: The metadata transmitted during the data flow contains identifying information about the parties.

title: Linking via Profiling
description: The mobile app backend processes the retrieved video clip and may perform profiling or inference on the data. This processing can reveal patterns or insights that link the video data to a specific individual or group of individuals, enabling the homeowner to identify the source.
assumptions: The backend performs processing that allows for the identification of the data subject.
